Looking at this problem, I need to systematically work through the logical constraints.

**Starting with what's certain:**
- Vernell tells the truth (given)
- Fletcher says "Vernell lies" → Since Vernell tells truth, Fletcher lies
- Tamika says exactly one of (Fletcher, Oakleigh, Oscar) tells truth. Since Fletcher lies and Oakleigh/Oscar always have opposite truth values (from their mutual contradictions), exactly one of the three tells truth → Tamika tells the truth

**Building the chain:**
- Ka says "either exactly 2 of (Tamika, Oleg, Mario) tell truth OR none"
  - Tamika tells truth
  - Oleg and Mario must have the same truth value (mutual affirmations)
  - Whether both true (3 total) or both false (1 total), neither condition is met → Ka lies

- Teressa says "Ka tells truth" → Since Ka lies, Teressa lies

- Andree says "either exactly 1 of (Teressa, Miles, Megan) tells truth OR all 3"
  - Teressa lies
  - Miles and Megan have the same truth value (mutual affirmations)
  - Whether both true (2 total) or both false (0 total), neither condition is met → Andree lies

- Willian says "Andree lies" → Since Andree lies, Willian tells truth

**Cascading truth values:**
- Alejandro says exactly 2 of (Willian, Ocean, Virginia) tell truth
  - Willian tells truth, Ocean/Virginia are opposites (1 of them) → exactly 2 total
  - Alejandro tells truth

- Sal says exactly 2 of (Alejandro, Mark, Micah) tell truth
  - Alejandro tells truth, Mark/Micah are opposites (1 of them) → exactly 2 total
  - Sal tells truth

- Shalonda says "Sal tells truth" → Shalonda tells truth

- Gwenn says exactly 2 of (Shalonda, Octavio, Osborn) tell truth
  - Shalonda tells truth, Octavio/Osborn are opposites (1 of them) → exactly 2 total
  - Gwenn tells truth

**For Conception:**
- Conception says "either all 3 of (Gwenn, Misty, Olivia) tell truth OR only 1"
  - Gwenn tells truth
  - Misty and Olivia have same truth value
  - If both true: 3 total (satisfies "all 3") 
  - If both false: 1 total (satisfies "only 1")
  - Either way, the condition is satisfied → **Conception tells truth**

**For Raymond:**
- Jamey says "either exactly 2 of (Conception, Otis, Millie) tell truth OR none"
  - Conception tells truth
  - Otis and Millie have same truth value
  - If both true: 3 total (neither condition met, Jamey lies)
  - If both false: 1 total (neither condition met, Jamey lies)
  - → Jamey lies

- Raymond says "either all 3 of (Jamey, Matteo, Melinda) lie OR 2 tell truth"
  - Jamey lies
  - Matteo and Melinda have same truth value
  - If both true: 2 tell truth (condition satisfied)
  - If both false: all 3 lie (condition satisfied)
  - Either way → **Raymond tells truth**

**For Alexis:**
- Ryan says "exactly 2 of (Raymond, Mina, Mike) tell truth"
  - Raymond tells truth, Mina/Mike are opposites (1 of them) → exactly 2 total
  - Ryan tells truth

- Alexis says "either all 3 of (Ryan, Osian, Mustafa) tell truth OR only 1"
  - Ryan tells truth
  - Osian and Mustafa have same truth value
  - If both true: 3 total (satisfies "all 3")
  - If both false: 1 total (satisfies "only 1")
  - Either way → **Alexis tells truth**

ANSWER: <yes, yes, yes>
